units.summary: ParseQuantity now canonicalizes and caches the string form on the two return paths that did not already set it. Parsed quantities carry q.s from creation, so later String() calls do not need to mutate them.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now always caches the canonical string
units.reason: Changes the state of every parsed Quantity (cached s field), which affects equality comparisons, encoding and concurrency behavior.
focus: every return path of ParseQuantity sets q.s (early returns, overflow/maxAllowed path)
callers or tests comparing parsed Quantity with reflect.DeepEqual against constructed ones
parse cost increase from canonicalizing eagerly

units.summary: String() no longer writes the computed string back into the receiver; it returns the cached value if present, otherwise computes it each time. This removes a data race on concurrent reads but makes String() on uncached quantities recompute every call.
units.headline: String() no longer mutates receiver and caches nothing
units.reason: Changes caching and mutation semantics of a widely used public method, with performance and concurrency consequences.
focus: hot paths that build Quantity via NewQuantity/Add/etc. and call String repeatedly
code or tests relying on String() populating q.s

units.summary: Adds exported CacheString, which computes the canonical string and always stores it on the receiver. Callers must own the instance since it writes.
units.headline: Add exported Quantity.CacheString that stores canonical string
units.reason: New public API that mutates the receiver, with concurrency contract on callers.
focus: CacheString is only called on instances not shared across goroutines
unconditional write is acceptable for callers holding shared read-only values

units.summary: The test now expects ParseQuantity to set the cached string and drops the check that String() populates q.s. The expectation was changed to match the new String() behavior.
units.headline: TestQuantityString expects parse-time caching, drops String-caching assertion
units.reason: Expectations were changed to match new behavior and an assertion was removed, which could hide a regression.
focus: the removed assertion is covered by the new ParseQuantity cache check and TestQuantityCacheString

units.summary: New test covering CacheString: it populates q.s, is idempotent, and returns <nil> for a nil receiver. It only exercises the new method.
units.headline: Add test for Quantity.CacheString
units.reason: New test only; cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: Benchmark rewritten to use sub-benchmarks per quantity with b.Loop, and the Precalc variant is removed. It affects only benchmarks.
units.headline: BenchmarkQuantityString restructured into per-value sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark restructured into per-value sub-benchmarks using b.Loop. It affects only benchmark code.
units.headline: BenchmarkQuantityStringBinarySI restructured into sub-benchmarks

units.summary: Benchmark now iterates the shared test cases as sub-benchmarks and no longer checks errors. It affects only benchmark code.
units.headline: BenchmarkParseQuantity uses shared test cases as sub-benchmarks
